title: Redwood POC scoping with SummitCare - security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security/compliance requirements for a 3-month pilot: SOC 2 / ISO certificates, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit logs retention, KMS integration and workload/benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send security pack and run a benchmarks plan; customer to provide sample workloads and compliance contact.
topics: hosting modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Ava, Diego - Redwood; Priya, Marcus, Ellen - SummitCare

Summary (auto): scoping call for security pilot; focus on SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and benchmark plan.

00:00 - Ava (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:06 - Priya (SummitCare): hi, this is priya, head of eng, im on.
00:09 - Marcus (SummitCare): marcus here, security arch.
00:11 - Ellen (SummitCare): ellen here, product.
00:13 - Diego (Redwood SE): diego, se, hi all.
00:15 - Ava: awesome, thanks. agenda is to align success criteria for the poc, confirm workload sizing and benchmarks, and then deep dive into the security asks — soc 2, iso, sso/saml, rbac, audit logs and kms.

02:02 - Priya: high level, our success metric is that the assistant meets throughput needs for triage workflows and does not exceed X latency targets. i think we said p95 under 450ms for the short prompts and probably under 700 for long context. that's like a number to start with. also cost targets matter.

03:10 - Ava: yep that tracks. for the pilot we usually measure p50/p95 latency, tokens per second throughput, and token cost. we'll propose a bench plan. diego, can you outline typical benchmark steps?

03:25 - Diego: sure. we'll run three phases: baseline small (1k msgs/day), scale test (10k/day) and peak load (concurrency sim). measure cold start vs warmed KV cache, and include quantized model variants. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and throughput qps, tokens/sec. for hosted vs dedicated we'll note differences.

04:40 - Marcus: question on data residency — we need logs and data retained in US only and some PHI considerations. we might need private deployment or dedicated with VPC.

05:05 - Ava: understood. SummitCare's PHI requirement likely pushes towards Dedicated or Private. for pilot we can do dedicated capacity in a US region; private on-prem is also doable but is heavier. we'll include both options in the pricing doc.

06:30 - Ellen: for compliance, procurement asked for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 docs, plus evidence of audit logs and SSO. you mentioned earlier you have certs?

06:45 - Ava: yes we have SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001 attestation. i'll send the certs and the security pack after this call.

08:02 - Priya: ok, can you confirm retention windows for audit logs and whether logs are immutable?

08:10 - Diego: our audit logs are write-once in the control plane with configurable retention; for Dedicated we can push audit logs to customer-owned S3 or a SIEM via syslog. retention policy is configurable — default 90 days but can be extended. logs are tamper-evident; we can provide chain-of-custody info in the security pack.

09:50 - Marcus: KMS — do you integrate with customer-managed keys? we need to ensure we can control encryption-at-rest keys.

10:02 - Ava: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Dedicated and Private. in Hosted we have platform keys but offer key-wrapping and bring-your-own-key options for certain tiers. i'll include the key management flow for each deployment mode.

11:20 - Priya: SSO — we use Okta. need SAML and SCIM provisioning, and ability to map groups to RBAC roles.

11:35 - Diego: we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based at team and route level; we can pre-map Okta groups to roles. for the pilot we can set up a test IdP in your dev Okta tenant.

12:12 - Ellen: is there an admin audit trail showing who invoked which model and which route? also token-level cost visibility?

12:25 - Diego: yes, our console provides per-route and per-token tracing, request-level metadata with user_id, route, model, tokens in/out. audit logs include user actions like role changes and API key creations.

14:00 - Speaker 1 (SummitCare): just to flag, legal will need a data processing addendum (DPA) and we may request subprocessor list.

14:12 - Ava: correct, we'll include DPA and current subprocessor list in the security pack.

15:00 - Priya: back to success criteria — besides latency we need quality gates. we'll share a small eval prompt set that must not regress compared to current system. if redwood's output fails our BLEU/Human eval thresholds then the import will fail.

15:22 - Diego: good call. include that eval set with expected pass/fail thresholds; we can run regen tests and track model regression. we also support automated evals and webhook alerts for regressions.

16:55 - Ellen: workforce access — we need RBAC that supports least privilege and separation of duties for ops vs dev. can you show example roles?

17:10 - Diego: example roles: Viewer, Developer, Operator, Admin. Operators can deploy rollouts, Developers can call the API and create prompts, Admins manage billing and keys. we can provide a role matrix mapping to Okta groups.

18:40 - Priya: benchmark details — what sample sizes and token lengths do you recommend? our triage requests average 80 tokens in, 120 tokens out, but some long context up to 2k tokens for patient history.

19:00 - Diego: that's helpful. we'll include sequences: short (<=128 tokens), medium (128-1024), and long (1k-2k). for concurrency tests we'll simulate 100 concurrent users with bursts to 500 for peak. qps baseline we'll test 30 qps scaling up to 200 qps depending on model.

20:40 - Marcus: for PHI we may require on-prem for some workloads. can Redwood run a split model where prompt processing occurs in our VPC and the control plane in Redwood?

21:00 - Ava: yes, we have a private control plane option and hybrid routing for sensitive prefixes — we can route sensitive requests to on-prem connectors while keeping telemetry minimal. we'll outline architecture options in the follow-up doc.

22:30 - Priya: timeline — we want a pilot start mid-March and 8-12 week pilot. can you support that?

23:00 - Ava: yes, mid-March start is feasible. immediate next week we'll sign an SOW for a 3-month pilot. first two weeks: infra + SSO + KMS config; weeks 3-4: run bench & quality evals; weeks 5-10: iterative tuning and canary with our app; final week: exit review and decision.

25:10 - Ellen: what are success exit criteria — ok to capture?

25:20 - Priya: success if p95 < 700ms for our medium prompts, throughput meets 80% of target qps, costs within agreed per-token budget, and no critical security blockers found in audit. and quality eval must meet pass thresholds on 90% of test cases.

26:40 - Diego: noted. we'll translate that into measurable runbooks and pass/fail gates.

28:30 - Marcus: one more on logging — do you support forwarder to our Splunk instance?

28:45 - Diego: yes splunk or sumo or any SIEM via syslog / forwarder. We can ship JSON payloads with request metadata.

30:00 - Speaker 2 (SummitCare): quick ask — can you provide a sample RBAC policy and audit log sample?

30:10 - Ava: yes we'll include sample logs, RBAC matrix, and event schema.

31:20 - Priya: for benchmarks, will you run them in our environment or Redwood's?

31:30 - Diego: two parts: initial synthetic benchmarks in Redwood hosted infra to set expectations; then we run a follow-up run in a dedicated tenant that mirrors your region and VPC. for PHI we prefer the dedicated tenant run in your VPC.

33:00 - Ellen: any limitations on model size or quantization we should know about for the pilot?

33:10 - Diego: we support common open model families; for long context use model X (ver 2) and for quantized variants we may see latency tradeoffs. we'll list recommended model/quantization combos per workload.

34:20 - Priya: can you outline what data is logged to telemetry vs what stays in customer data plane?

34:35 - Diego: telemetry aggregates usage and performance metrics (tokens, latency) with no PII by default. request-level payloads and raw prompts stay in the customer data plane for Dedicated/Private; in Hosted they are logged for debugging but can be disabled and routed to customer storage if required. we'll document exact fields.

36:00 - Marcus: procurement will want indemnities and subprocessor recourse, that will be part of contract discussion.

36:15 - Ava: understood. we'll loop legal.

37:30 - Ellen: Ok next steps recap?

37:40 - Ava: recap: (1) Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, ISO certs, DPA, subprocessor list), (2) Diego to deliver benchmark plan and sample logs + RBAC matrix, (3) SummitCare to share sample workloads, eval prompts, Okta test tenant access, and compliance contact, (4) schedule follow-up technical runbook and pilot start date.

39:00 - Priya: timeline to send docs? ideally by Friday next week.

39:10 - Ava: we'll aim to send security pack and SSO steps by 2026-03-06. diego will send benchmark plan by 2026-03-09.

40:00 - Speaker 1 (SummitCare): small transcription note — sorry if interruptions, hope audio ok.

40:10 - Diego: audio's fine.

41:00 - Ellen: pricing — can you give a rough pilot price for dedicated capacity?

41:15 - Ava: rough ballpark in the follow-up pricing doc; for a 3-month pilot with dedicated capacity we typically size to expected qps and offer a discounted reserved rate. we'll include hosted vs dedicated cost examples.

43:20 - Priya: good. any competitors or gotchas we should be aware of?

43:30 - Ava: many customers compare to Anthropic and Bedrock for managed endpoints and to self-hosts for cost control; pros/cons depend on control plane needs and compliance requirements. we'll include a short competitive note.

45:00 - Marcus: ok thanks. we'll expect docs and to schedule the first setup call. legal will reach out for DPA.

45:10 - Ava: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with attachments and a calendar invite for the next call.

46:00 - Meeting ends.
